bib.title: Beyond Examples: High-level Automated Reasoning Paradigm in In-Context Learning via MCTS

read.skipped: Reference list (arXiv v2, 2 Jun 2025) skimmed only for lineage.

question: Can in-context learning be improved by supplying abstract, automatically searched reasoning patterns instead of concrete demonstration examples?
hypothesis: Teaching a model high-level reasoning patterns (thought cards) matched to problem complexity generalises better and costs less than example-based ICL or per-question tree search.
contributions: Extend ICL 'context' from specific examples to abstract high-level reasoning patterns
MCTS-powered framework that builds diverse reasoning patterns and applies them adaptively by problem attributes
80.6% MATH and 62.5% AMC with Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, above GPT-4o, with about 10x lower time cost than leading test-time inference methods

method.summary: Offline, MCTS over five atomic reasoning actions (SA, OST, CoT, DC, SRR) runs on 200 seed training questions; the best path per question (reward minus cost) is distilled into thought cards keyed by problem complexity. Online, the 5 nearest cards by complexity attributes guide the model's generation, candidates are scored by a process reward model, and the top 3 get a self-consistency vote.
method.task: multi-step reasoning (math, arithmetic, commonsense, science QA) by inference-time prompting with searched reasoning templates

other.use: computes SC, PCC, PS attributes of test questions (Sec 2.2)

other.note: off-the-shelf RLHFlow checkpoints; PRM is default

other.use: weak model building cards in weak-to-strong test

inference.samples: MCTS-time details: expansion samples n actions (n not stated); inference uses 5 nearest thought cards, top-3 paths after PRM go to self-consistency; no repeated runs or seeds stated; baseline CoT+SC@4
inference.prompting: Thought card (sequence of atomic actions, e.g. SA->OST->CoT) given as natural-language instruction; model must end with 'The answer is'
inference.retrieval: Nearest-neighbour match of test question's PCC (default), SC or PS against card averages; abs. difference for SC and PCC, cosine similarity for PS; 5 cards

other.reward: leaf reward = confidence (likelihood) of self-consistency majority vote; no learned reward in search

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: strict match of final answer ('The answer is') to ground truth

metrics.name: average time cost per sample
metrics.definition: offline card construction time plus online inference time, per test sample (Eq 8)

eval.protocol: Single reported number per cell; no seeds, variance or significance tests stated. Tree-method and closed-model numbers mostly copied from original papers; ICL baselines run by the authors; others reproduced with official code when available.

limits: No variance, seeds or repeated runs are reported; AMC has 40 problems (one problem = 2.5 points).
Comparisons to GPT-4o and tree methods mix self-run and copied numbers; 'few-shot GPT-4o 77.2' in Sec 4.1 is actually the CoT+SC@4 row in Table 1 (few-shot CoT is 76.6).
Number of MCTS iterations, children per expansion n, the discount alpha, and the GRPO/SFT recipes behind Tables 5 and 14 are not given.

Authors concede: more thought cards improve accuracy but add overhead and 'finding an optimal balance' is future work; SC, PCC and PS contribute 'minimal statistical variations' so PCC is used and richer combinations are left open; action space tuning per domain left for future work.
Offline cost is fixed per seed set (200 samples) and amortised; time comparison is against rStar etc. on Llama3-8B only.
Distilling a single best path per question into an average-attribute template discards the question content; AMC and GPQA seeds come from the MATH training set (cross-domain).
Seed questions at test-time come from the train split of the same benchmark, so cards are task-tuned except in the OOD and weak-to-strong tests.
